text: The functional definition of cognition used throughout this book identifies a three-part 'SIA' architecture as the minimal structure of any cognitive process. What are its three components?
explanation: The book defines cognition functionally as the sensing-integrating-acting (SIA) triad: detecting relevant signals, combining them (possibly with stored information), and producing behavior directed by that combined assessment. 'Perceiving-reasoning-speaking' describes anthropocentric higher cognition; 'stimulus-response-reward' is behaviorist conditioning; 'encoding-storing-retrieving' is the memory-systems model, only one facet of cognition.
